## What it is

A personal budgeting app based on envelope budgeting: every unit of income is given a job, and spending is tracked against it. It is local-first: the budget lives on each device and the server syncs it between devices, serves the web app, and connects to bank-sync providers (GoCardless, SimpleFIN). Upstream: "A local-first personal finance app" (https://actualbudget.org/docs/install/).

**Icon:** `icon.svg` is a neutral initials icon from the scaffolder. The upstream logo is white on a transparent background and would be invisible on a light Market card.

## How it is packaged

- **Image:** `actualbudget/actual-server` on Docker Hub, the image upstream documents (https://actualbudget.org/docs/install/docker). It is built from `packages/sync-server/docker/ubuntu.Dockerfile` by upstream's `docker-release.yml`. The same digest is also published as `ghcr.io/actualbudget/actual`.
- **Security:** the image sets no `USER`, so by default it runs as root. Its Dockerfile creates the user `actual` (UID/GID 1001) and makes it the owner of `/data`, so the pod runs as 1001 with `runAsNonRoot`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, all Linux capabilities dropped, `RuntimeDefault` seccomp and no service-account token.
- **State:** one PVC `actual-budget-data` (1 Gi, the cluster default class) on `/data`. The server keeps `server-files/account.sqlite` (the hashed server password, the file list and sessions) and `user-files/` (the budget files) there. One replica with the `Recreate` strategy, so two pods never write the SQLite files at once.
- **Network:** Service `actual-budget`, port 5006 (HTTP), the upstream default.
- **Health:** startup, readiness and liveness probes on `GET /health`, which returns 200 `{"status":"UP"}` (`packages/sync-server/src/app.ts`). Upstream's compose health check calls the same route.

**Sizing:** upstream publishes no sizing guidance. Measured on 2026-11-12 (app-gate smoke run, k3s v1.37.2+k3s1, arm64): 145 Mi and 1m CPU at idle with no budget loaded, so the request is 160 Mi. The 512 Mi limit leaves room for syncing and bank-sync imports.

## First run

From the upstream docs (https://actualbudget.org/docs/install/docker, https://actualbudget.org/docs/config/https, https://actualbudget.org/docs/getting-started/sync):

1. Open the app's web UI (port 5006) from the OneMind dashboard.
2. On first open the server asks you to **set a server password** (checked in the smoke run: `/account/needs-bootstrap` answers `bootstrapped: false` on a fresh install). There is no default login. Anyone who can reach the port before you set it can set it, so do this right after install.
3. Create a new budget file or import one. The browser keeps a local copy and syncs it to this server.
4. Optional: turn on **end-to-end encryption** in the budget's settings. The server then cannot read the budget. Upstream warns that a forgotten encryption password cannot be recovered.

**HTTPS:** upstream says HTTPS is needed "to safely use all of Actual's features", except when you open it through `localhost`. From another device, put it behind HTTPS (for example a Tailscale HTTPS name or a reverse proxy; https://actualbudget.org/docs/config/reverse-proxies) rather than plain `http://<box>:5006`.
